meta.title: The Connected Peerless Fence: Your AI Integration Roadmap
meta.subtitle: From manual lead-to-job handoffs to an automated, audit-ready workflow across HD Portal, Salesforce, and ComputerEase

strategicContext.summary: Peerless Fence is a specialty contractor providing residential and commercial fence installation services, operating through the Home Depot Service Center Portal as its primary sales channel and using ComputerEase (Deltek) for job costing and project management. The company is an SMB operating brand within the Elevate Fence Partners platform, backed by Akoya Capital, with an integration scope spanning six-plus systems and no in-house MuleSoft development capability. The sharpest blocker to go-live is enabling ComputerEase API access and configuring the CE Live Service relay — without it, no automated job creation or project sync is possible.
strategicContext.operatingBrandPositioning: Peerless Fence provides residential and commercial fence installation services, sourcing leads through the Home Depot Service Center Portal and managing job execution through ComputerEase.
strategicContext.lattice: Peerless Fence operates as an SMB brand within the Elevate Fence Partners platform, which is sponsored by Akoya Capital.
strategicContext.whyNow: Two blockers are on the critical path right now: first, ComputerEase API access must be enabled and the CE Live Service relay configured — a Deltek support ticket that must be submitted before any job-creation automation can be built or tested. Second, GCP firewall rules currently allow SSH and RDP access from anywhere ('They're allowing SSH and RDP from anywhere, which is really bad practice') — hardening those rules is a prerequisite to safely exposing the ComputerEase VM to any integration layer.

challenge.lead: Every manual handoff between HD Portal, Salesforce, and ComputerEase is a silent failure waiting to happen — and the security exposure underneath it makes it worse. 'There's no firewall. They could put in a username and password and keep trying and trying and trying until they get in.' The goal of Stage 1 is simple: close the exposure, stabilize the data flow, and make sure nothing breaks quietly.

cards.label: Ashley's Morning Queue
cards.text: Ashley manually checks the HD Portal backend every morning to find new leads, then re-enters them into Salesforce — a process that delays consultation scheduling and introduces transcription errors on every lead that comes through the Home Depot channel.

cards.label: Job Entry Is a Hand-Off Chain
cards.text: When a Salesforce opportunity closes, Ashley manually creates the customer record in ComputerEase, enters deposit amounts and payment terms from the HD Portal contract, and then uploads signed contract documents (299A, 299B, 118) into the ComputerEase job record — each step a separate manual touch with no automated validation.

cards.label: Security Exposure on the ComputerEase VM
cards.text: 'There's no firewall. They could put in a username and password and keep trying and trying and trying until they get in' — the GCP instance hosting ComputerEase currently allows SSH and RDP from any IP address, meaning the job-costing system is reachable by anyone on the internet.

cards.label: ComputerEase API Is Not Yet Active
cards.text: 'It's an ancient system... I feel like I've traveled back to the 90s' — ComputerEase API access has not been enabled with Deltek, the CE Live Service relay is not configured, and API version compatibility (v26+) has not been confirmed, blocking every automated flow in this proposal until a support ticket is resolved.

solution.lead: DataSkate places a MuleSoft managed layer between HD Portal, Salesforce, ComputerEase, and DocHub — handling retry logic, dead-letter queuing, and operational monitoring that native point-to-point connections do not provide. The comparison is not cost — it's what you own after the project closes. The lower quote transfers ownership back to you on day 31.
solution.diagramCaption: DataSkate-managed MuleSoft layer — no code changes required in Salesforce or ComputerEase. Bidirectional flows (UC1, UC6) noted: ComputerEase job status syncs back to Salesforce sales orders in addition to outbound job creation.

roi.headline: The business case for moving now
roi.body: Peerless Fence runs 6+ systems — HD Portal, Salesforce, ComputerEase, DocHub, GCP, and Deltek — with no automated handoffs between them. Ashley manually checks HD Portal every morning, re-keys lead data into Salesforce, then re-enters job details into ComputerEase by hand. Every closed deal that touches all three systems is a manual relay race with no error detection until something breaks downstream.

journey.headline: The path to: 'I think by next early next week, I think we should be able to figure out all the access connectivity and extracting data. So we should be good after that.'

stage1.label: Stage 1
stage1.headline: Lead Ingestion & Qualification via HD Portal → Salesforce
items: HD Portal leads land in Salesforce automatically every 10 minutes — no more manual morning check by Ashley; the HD F-number becomes the external ID that prevents duplicates
Appointment scheduling syncs from HD Portal to Salesforce calendar without manual re-entry
Quote details verified and entered into Salesforce opportunity automatically when a sales rep closes in HD Portal — Ashley's manual verification step stops on go-live day
GCP firewall rules hardened to restrict SSH/RDP access before any integration goes live — the security exposure flagged in discovery is closed first
Salesforce API user permissions confirmed and sandbox environment validated to match production — no surprises during UAT

stage2.label: Stage 2
stage2.headline: Quote-to-Job Workflow: Salesforce → ComputerEase with Contract Validation
items: When a Salesforce opportunity is saved as final, a new job, customer record, and budget worksheet are created in ComputerEase automatically — manual data entry by Ashley is eliminated
Customer record creation in ComputerEase is triggered by HD Portal lead data — no more manual re-keying from lead to job
Contract documents (299A, 299B, 118) routed through DocHub for digital signature capture; signed documents attached to the ComputerEase job record without manual upload
Deposit amount and payment terms from HD Portal contract entered into ComputerEase job maintenance automatically — Ashley's manual deposit entry step is removed
ComputerEase job status attached to Salesforce sales order automatically after job creation — no manual linking step required

stage3.label: Stage 3
stage3.headline: Project Execution & Compliance Automation via ComputerEase API & IDP
items: ComputerEase API (CE Live Service relay, v26+) enabled — task creation, material ordering, and labor scheduling triggered automatically from Salesforce project data; Barb's manual material ordering step in Salesforce is replaced

Intelligent Document Processing extracts contract data from 299A, 299B, and 118 documents and validates against business rules — permit dates, deposit amounts, and signature legibility checked automatically; exceptions flagged for Ashley's review rather than full manual review of every document
Read-only Salesforce sync from ComputerEase provides project status visibility to sales reps and coordinators — Clayton and Jeff see job progress in Salesforce without logging into ComputerEase
Automated deposit verification from HD Portal backend triggers job entry in ComputerEase without Ashley manually checking backend reporting — when the deposit clears, the job moves forward
Quote line items from Salesforce validated against ComputerEase master data (material type, picket type, post caps, gates) before job creation — discrepancies flagged before they become field errors

journey.closingLine: The managed service model means DataSkate absorbs the operational risk — you get the outcomes without owning the infrastructure that delivers them.

nextSteps.title: Fill Out Intake Form
nextSteps.body: Complete the intake form so DataSkate can confirm system access, API credentials, and environment details before the technical deep dive. This is the fastest way to unblock the five P0 items identified in discovery — ComputerEase API enablement, GCP firewall hardening, Salesforce permissions, HD Portal credentials from Marius, and DocHub configuration.

nextSteps.title: Schedule Technical Deep Dive
nextSteps.body: Book a working session with Raghuram Potluri to walk through the ComputerEase CE Live Service relay configuration, GCP firewall rule changes, and Salesforce sandbox parity. This session resolves the connectivity blockers so API testing can begin the following week.

nextSteps.title: Review Integration Deck
nextSteps.body: The integration deck maps all 12 confirmed flows across HD Portal, Salesforce, ComputerEase, DocHub, and GCP — with complexity ratings and sequencing. Review it before the SOW call so the scope conversation starts from a shared picture of what gets built in each stage.

nextSteps.title: Align on Scope and SOW
nextSteps.body: Once the intake form is complete and the integration deck is reviewed, DataSkate will issue a Statement of Work covering Stage 1 flows, IaaS managed connector configuration, field mapping, error handling, UAT support, and 30-day hypercare. No surprises — every line item is traceable to a confirmed flow from the discovery session.

flows.name: Job Entry with Budget Data: Salesforce → ComputerEase

flows.name: Customer Record Creation: HD Portal → ComputerEase

flows.name: Contract Generation & Digital Signature: Salesforce → DocHub
flows.value: Contract documents (types 299A, 299B, 118) are generated from Salesforce opportunity data and routed to DocHub for digital signature capture — replacing the manual document prep and routing step.

flows.name: Quote Entry: HD Portal → Salesforce

flows.value: Quote details created in HD Portal flow into Salesforce opportunities automatically. Ashley's manual verification and re-entry step is removed from the process.

flows.name: Job Status Attachment: ComputerEase → Salesforce
flows.value: ComputerEase project and work order records are linked to Salesforce sales orders automatically after job entry — eliminating Ashley's manual attachment step.

flows.value: GCP firewall rules are configured to restrict API access to the ComputerEase VM to authorized sources only — closing the open SSH/RDP exposure identified during scoping and enabling secure integration traffic.

outcomes.title: Ashley's Manual Queue — Cleared
outcomes.body: Lead verification, customer record creation, contract uploads, deposit entry, and task assignment were all manual steps owned by one person. On go-live day, the scheduled and event-driven flows handle each of these automatically — Ashley's queue shrinks to exception handling only.

outcomes.title: Secure, Auditable API Access
outcomes.body: GCP firewall rules are hardened to restrict SSH/RDP access to authorized sources. ComputerEase API access is enabled through Deltek with sandbox/production parity. Every integration call is logged — the open exposure identified during scoping is closed before the first flow goes live.

outcomes.title: AI-Ready Foundation
outcomes.body: Clean, connected, well-maintained data infrastructure is what AI agents need to operate. Every flow we build is a pipeline an AI agent will eventually use — built right from the start.

included.title: 12 Integration Flows — Built & Maintained
included.detail: All 12 confirmed flows (UC1–UC12) across HD Portal, Salesforce, ComputerEase, DocHub, GCP, and Deltek — designed, built, tested, and maintained by DataSkate for the duration of the engagement.

included.title: MuleSoft Hosting & Runtime Management
included.detail: DataSkate manages the MuleSoft CloudHub runtime environment — provisioning, patching, uptime monitoring, and capacity management are included. Peerless Fence does not own or operate the middleware layer.

included.title: Field Mapping & Data Transformation
included.detail: All field-level mapping between HD Portal, Salesforce, ComputerEase, and DocHub — including HD F-number external ID keying, contract type routing (299A, 299B, 118), and budget worksheet field alignment.

included.title: Error Handling & Retry Logic
included.detail: Every flow includes structured error handling with retry logic and alerting. When a sync fails, the system retries automatically and notifies the team — failures surface loudly rather than silently dropping records.

included.title: UAT Support & Integration Testing
included.detail: DataSkate supports Peerless Fence through two weeks of user acceptance testing — including sandbox-to-production validation for ComputerEase, Salesforce, and HD Portal flows.

included.title: 30-Day Hypercare Post Go-Live
included.detail: Dedicated support for 30 days after go-live — priority response to any flow failures, field mapping corrections, or credential rotation issues that arise in the production environment.

oos.title: ComputerEase CE Live Service Enablement (Deltek Vendor Action)
oos.detail: Submitting and managing the Deltek support ticket to enable API access and configure the CE Live Service relay is a client and vendor action. DataSkate will validate connectivity once access is confirmed, but cannot initiate or expedite the Deltek support process.

oos.title: GCP Firewall Hardening (Client IT Action)
oos.detail: Restricting SSH/RDP access on the ComputerEase VM and configuring network isolation within GCP is the responsibility of Peerless Fence's IT team or GCP administrator. DataSkate will specify the required IP allowlist but does not administer the client's GCP environment.

oos.title: HD Portal API Credential Procurement (Home Depot Vendor Action)
oos.detail: Obtaining API credentials from the Home Depot Portal team (Marius) is a client-to-vendor coordination task. DataSkate cannot access or request HD Portal credentials on behalf of Peerless Fence.

oos.title: DocHub Account Configuration & Signature Template Setup
oos.detail: Configuring DocHub to capture digital signatures for contract types 299A, 299B, and 118 — including template design and document storage settings — is a client action. DataSkate integrates with a configured DocHub instance; it does not administer the DocHub account.

oos.title: Salesforce Object Design & Custom Field Configuration
oos.detail: Any changes to Salesforce object schema, custom field creation, page layout updates, or permission set design are outside this engagement. DataSkate maps to existing Salesforce fields; structural Salesforce configuration is a client or Salesforce admin responsibility.

oos.title: Historical Data Migration
oos.detail: This engagement covers net-new data from go-live forward. Migration of historical job records, customer records, or contract documents from HD Portal or ComputerEase into Salesforce is not included.

oos.title: HD Portal Test Lead Management
oos.detail: Creating, managing, or cleaning up test leads in the HD Portal sandbox environment for UAT purposes is a Peerless Fence responsibility. DataSkate will specify the test data requirements but does not operate within the HD Portal backend.

GCP firewall rules for the ComputerEase VM are hardened to restrict SSH/RDP access to authorized IP addresses only. Network isolation is configured before integration testing begins.

HD Portal API credentials are obtained from the Home Depot Portal team (Marius). Polling mechanism (10-minute frequency) or webhook endpoint is confirmed and accessible from DataSkate's MuleSoft environment.
assumptions.when: Before Week 1 (blocks UC1, UC3, UC5, UC7, UC9, UC12)

assumptions.assumption: DocHub is configured to capture digital signatures for contract types 299A, 299B, and 118. A document storage and retrieval API endpoint is available for Salesforce integration.
A dedicated DataSkate integration user is provisioned in Salesforce with API-only access and a non-expiring credential. A read-only API user is established in ComputerEase for status sync flows.
Jean Jacobs (ComputerEase Administrator) and Brian Cook (Infrastructure/Systems Administrator) are available for technical coordination during Discovery and UAT phases.
Ashley Salerno is available to validate flow outputs during UAT — confirming that lead records, job entries, customer records, and contract documents match expected results.
